title: EGI Node - EGI
main_text: EGI for EOSC EGI Node Operated by the EGI Foundation on behalf of the EGI Federation, the Node provides scalable compute, storage, data management and advanced digital research services for data-intensive science. It delivers EOSC Core and Federating Capabilities including AAI, catalogue, monitoring, accounting, helpdesk and application deployment management, while supporting multi-node use cases in reproducible workflows, AI, sensitive data analysis, machine learning and federated LLM services. EGI for EOSC Objectives Impact Status Access the EGI Node Capabilities Coordination Key Objective in Capacity as a Node To act as a Node for data-intensive computing and large-scale research data exploitation, enabling seamless, cross-border access to FAIR data, advanced analytics, AI/ML models, compute, storage, workflow and federating capabilities for EOSC. Impact Science Areas The EGI Node is multidisciplinary, operating in the following areas: Data-intensive science Cloud computing High-throughput computing High-performance computing Artificial Intelligence and machine learning Cross-disciplinary research Scientific Impact EGI enables large-scale interdisciplinary data exploitation by combining compute, storage, workflows, data services, AI/ML models and EOSC federating capabilities across a distributed European infrastructure. Use Cases Reproducible workflows AI validation on sensitive health data Cross-node machine learning pipelines Federated LLM services Large-scale cross-node data processing FAIR Data Scientific datasets accessible through EGI DataHub and integrated NGI/RI resources. Domain data services such as EODC Data Catalog, HAL, Recherche Data Gouv, FAIDare API, WeNMR, DATAlife, yProvStore and PITHIA e-Science. FAIR-enabling services for data access, transfer, storage, provenance and reuse. Status The EGI Node currently has the status of Candidate Node. Technical status Federated AAI Onboarded service catalogues (EGI catalogue; NGI and RI service resources) Application workflow management Service monitoring Service and research product accounting Order management Helpdesk Management system Timeline and milestones Phased deployment roadmap for 2026-2027, with use cases expanded through EOSC Mesh and ongoing operation of EOSC federating capabilities. Deliverables Project charter Integration with Federating Capabilities: AAI and Catalogue Application Deployment Management API – Software Release Report: Use cases – Lessons learnt and next steps Integration with Federating Capabilities: Helpdesk, Monitoring, SMS Stakeholders and communities’ engagement strategy EOSC Mesh Cross-Node use case analysis and implementation plan How to access the node Services are offered to European researchers under EGI Access Policy or service-specific access policies, including open, quota-based, project-based or cost access depending on service. children.main_text: Terms of Use This Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use (“AUP”) defines the rules and conditions that govern your access to and use (including transmission, processing, and storage of data) of the resources and services (“Services”) as granted by the EGI Federation, and the Virtual Organisation to which you belong, for the purpose of meeting the goals of EGI, namely to deliver advanced computing services to support researchers, multinational projects and research infrastructures, and the goals of your Virtual Organisation or Research Community. You shall only use the Services in a manner consistent with the purposes and limitations described above; you shall show consideration towards other users including by not causing harm to the Services; you have an obligation to collaborate in the resolution of issues arising from your use of the Services. You shall only use the Services for lawful purposes and not breach, attempt to breach, nor circumvent administrative or security controls. You shall respect intellectual property and confidentiality agreements. You shall protect your access credentials (e.g. passwords, private keys or multi-factor tokens); no intentional sharing is permitted. You shall keep your registered information correct and up to date. You shall promptly report known or suspected security breaches, credential compromise, or misuse to the security contact stated below; and report any compromised credentials to the relevant issuing authorities. Reliance on the Services shall only be to the extent specified by any applicable service level agreements listed below. Use without such agreements is at your own risk. Your personal data will be processed in accordance with the privacy statements referenced below. Your use of the Services may be restricted or suspended, for administrative, operational, or security reasons, without prior notice and without compensation. If you violate these rules, you may be liable for the consequences, which may include your account being suspended and a report being made to your home organisation or to law enforcement. The administrative contact for this AUP is: operations@egi.eu The security contact for this AUP is: abuse@egi.eu The privacy policy (e.g. Privacy Notice) is located at www.egi.eu/privacy-policy/ . children.title: About - EGI
children.main_text: EGI: Open Ecosystem for Research and Innovation We support data-intensive research with a wide range of advanced computing services EGI is the federation of computing and storage resource providers united by a mission of delivering advanced computing and data analytics services for research and innovation. Discover our services Learn about EGI Federation The "EGIverse" EGI Federation EGI is a federation of computing and storage resource providers united by a mission of delivering advanced computing and data analytics services for research and innovation. EGI Foundation EGI Foundation is a not-for-profit organisation created to coordinate and develop the EGI infrastructure and engage diverse users of our broad service portfolio. EGI Community The EGI community is a community of researchers, developers, funders, technologists, dreamers and do-ers : in short anyone with a stake in advanced computing for research. Impact "We continuously innovate our services and technology to meet the needs of researchers worldwide." [names removed] / Director of EGI Foundation The impact of the EGI Federation is broad and diverse. We support all kinds of research. Examples include finding new tools to diagnose and monitor diseases such as Alzheimer’s, developing complex simulations to model climate change, searching for gravitational waves, and pursuing the dark matter. We continuously innovate our services and technology, foster international collaborations and knowledge sharing, and finally, create opportunities for professional development and acquiring know-how. Annual Report 2025 How 1 1 Engage and Support User Communities We care about our users. EGI works with user communities to identify their needs, provide appropriate support and drive innovation together. 2 2 Design, Develop and Deploy Solutions We are here to find the best solutions. EGI offers high-quality, tailored consultation and technology services for the demanding needs of every research community and sector. 3 3 Serve, Support and Improve Services We strive to deliver the best possible services. We regularly review the satisfaction of our users and constantly innovate and evolve our service offering to meet the needs of all the user communities. 4 4 Influence Policies We help to shape the future. EGI advises policymakers and funders on the main trends and needs in science and technology and provides recommendations on the future directions. We strongly promote the vision for the Open Science Commons. 5 5 Run Our Services in a Sustainable Way We care about the future. EGI works towards long term, sustainable funding for operating EGI core services. At the same time, we raise funds for innovation, explore different business models while improving discoverability and reuse of services and solutions. EGI and EOSC EGI Supports a Web of FAIR Data and Services for Science in Europe European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) is an environment for hosting and processing research data to support EU science. The European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) initiative will offer researchers a virtual environment with open and seamless services for storage, management, analysis and re-use of research data, across borders and scientific disciplines by federating existing data infrastructures. EOSC is being co-created in a series of funded projects and initiatives from member states and associated countries. The services and expertise of the EGI Federation are being recognised as key assets for the EOSC, especially for the Federating Core. children.main_text: Services for Research Our large-scale Computing and Data Analytics Services are helping Scientists to accelerate the process leading to Research Outputs. Our services are provided by EGI’s federated cloud providers and data centres. They can be requested by everyone involved in research. What you can do Success stories Compute Compute Orchestration Storage & Data Security & Identity Applications Training Get Access EGI Access Call With this Access Call, EGI offers its services and related user support and training to individual researchers, national and international research projects, research communities, research infrastructures and commercial research entities. Submit your application Compute EGI compute infrastructure provides fast and flexible compute capacity to fit any research need, from Cloud compute to Cloud Container compute, and High-Throughput compute. Our Software Distribution enables users to publish and access software across multiple sites. Did you know? Cloud Compute Run virtual machines on demand with complete control over computing resources More info Cloud Container Compute Run Docker containers in a lightweight virtualised environment More info High-Throughput Compute Execute thousands of computational tasks to analyse large datasets More info Software Distribution Publish and access software efficiently across multiple sites More info Compute Orchestration Compute Orchestration is designed to give you complete control over your computing resources across the EGI distributed infrastructure. Our services maximise the efficiency of your computing operations, streamline your workload management, and boost your productivity. Did you know? Our Workload Manager ensures the computing tasks are managed and distributed efficiently while maximising the use of resources. During the last 12 months 12.5 Million jobs were running in total with peaks of more than 12,400 concurrent jobs. Workload Manager Manage computing workloads in an efficient way More info Infrastructure Manager Use cloud orchestrator to deploy and configure complex virtual infrastructures More info Storage and Data Do you need reliable services for storing and transferring your data across international research teams? With three specialised services to choose from, we have everything that users and service providers might need to store, share, and transfer their valuable data in a reliable and efficient way. Did you know? Over 580 PB online storage capacity is offered by HTC and Cloud storage providers. Online Storage Store, share and access your files and their metadata on a global scale More info Data Transfer Transfer large sets of data from one place to another More info DataHub Access key scientific datasets in a scalable way More info Security & Identity EGI Check-in enables single sign-in through different Identity Providers across multiple services. It acts as a central hub that connects federated Identity Providers to many service providers. Did you know? EGI Check-in serves as a seamless bridge, enabling more than 17,500 registered users to access 150+ services effortlessly, using their own institutional identity providers and community AAI services. Check-in Login with your own credentials More info Secrets Store Easily retrieve, manage, and rotate credentials, API keys, and other secrets through their lifecycle More info Applications With EGI Applications, you can gain access to online applications, application-hosting frameworks, and a browser-based tool for compute-intensive data analysis. Our innovative services offer a range of features and benefits that will transform the way you work with data. Did you know? Every month, more than 200 registered users from 32 countries make use of our Notebooks in over 100 sessions. Notebooks Create interactive documents with live code, visualisations and text More info Replay Reproduce and share research on a notebooks-based platform More info Training At EGI, we believe in empowering scientific communities through professional development and the acquisition of knowledge. We offer a wide range of training and consultancy services to help you make the most of our cutting-edge EGI services. Did you know? In 2022, EGI captivated over 500 attendees with a series of eight engaging webinars and nine comprehensive training sessions. Our training programme enabled over 1000 individuals to attain FitSM certifications. FitSM Training Learn how to manage IT services with a pragmatic and lightweight standard More info ISO 27001 Training Learn how to manage and secure information assets More info Training Infrastructure Dedicated computing and storage for training and education More info See other services Services for Federation EGI Digital Innovation Hub Services for Business Access Policies We strive to lower the entry barrier to access high-end services and professional support to all researchers. Thanks to the capability of integrating national and European investments, we can optimise the use of financial resources across borders and among disciplines. In most cases, we offer services free at the point of use. When it is not possible, we revert to paid access. For special needs, we can also channel community funding to our providers. Our ultimate goal is to lower the financial barrier to using the services for end users while ensuring that involved professionals and deployed computing infrastructures are compensated. children.main_text: Privacy Notice for Surveys The EGI Surveys service (hereinafter referred to as: "the service" or "Surveys") allows individuals to take part in surveys managed and conducted by EGI Foundation. This privacy notice describes how we, the EGI Foundation (hereinafter referred to as "we" or "the Data Controller"), collect and process data by which you can be personally identified ("Personal Data") when you use the service. EGI Foundation runs surveys on more than one platform. Each survey states which platform it uses. In addition to the information below, any survey form will include more specific information on what happens with the answers submitted through it, how and how long they will be stored, and who will gain access to them. Where a survey's own statement differs from this policy on a point specific to that survey, the survey's statement is the more specific one and applies. Taking part in an EGI survey is voluntary. You may stop at any point before you submit, and you may decline to answer any question that is not marked as required. Data controller The EGI Foundation Science Park 140 1098 XG Amsterdam The Netherlands Data protection officer The EGI Foundation Data Protection Officer Science Park 140 1098 XG Amsterdam The Netherlands E-mail: dpo@egi.eu Jurisdiction and supervisory authority Jurisdiction: NL, The Netherlands. EGI Foundation's lead supervisory authority is the Dutch Data Protection Authority. They can be contacted at autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl . Personal data processed The service may process the following personal data. Identification data Name E-mail address IP address, where the platform records it. On Formbricks, EGI Foundation configures its surveys so that the IP address is not stored with the response. Your IP address is still processed briefly while the connection is made, and is discarded rather than saved. Other identification data as far as captured by the individual survey Behavioural data, data allowing conclusions on the personality, biographical data, sociodemographic data Data on login, access and usage of the survey site (survey.egi.eu) Technical data recorded with a response: the country you responded from, your browser, operating system and device type, the web address of the page where you completed the survey, the date and time you started and submitted, and the progress you made, including partial responses Other data in these categories are only processed as far as they are captured by the individual survey Data carried in the survey link Some invitation links carry information in the web address so that we do not have to ask you for it again, for example a project code or a reference identifying you as an invited participant. Where a link carries such information, it is stored with your response, and the survey says so. EGI surveys do not request special categories of personal data (Article 9 GDPR). Where a specific survey needs to ask such a question, it will say so, explain why, and ask for your separate explicit consent before you answer. How personal data is collected Directly from you. Everything you enter into a survey, and any file you attach where a survey allows it. Automatically, when you respond. The technical data described above, generated by the platform as your browser communicates with it. From the invitation. Where we already hold your e-mail address, because you are an EGI Foundation contact, a project partner, a member of a community mailing list, or a registered participant in an EGI event, we may use it to invite you to a survey. Every invitation says how we obtained your address and how to stop receiving them. We do not buy personal data and we do not obtain it from data brokers or scraped sources. Anonymous and identified surveys We run both kinds, and each survey states which it is. An anonymous survey collects no name, no e-mail address and no other direct identifier. The technical data listed above is still recorded, so a response is not anonymous in the strict sense of the GDPR: a combination of country, organisation type, role and free-text answers can in principle identify someone in a small population. We treat all survey responses as personal data and protect them accordingly, and we describe a survey as anonymous only in the sense that we do not ask who you are. An identified survey asks for your name or e-mail address and states at that point why it needs them. When we publish or report survey results, we publish aggregated figures and anonymised quotations. Where we want to attribute a quotation to you by name or by organisation, we ask you first. Cookies What is placed on your device depends on the platform the survey uses. Formbricks : no cookies are set. The platform may use your browser's local storage to remember your progress within a long survey. Local storage stays on your device. LimeSurvey (survey.egi.eu) : a session cookie is set to keep your place in the survey, together with a cookie used to route your connection within the hosting. Both are strictly necessary to deliver the survey. Google Forms : Google sets its own cookies, governed by Google's privacy policy. We do not use advertising, profiling, cross-site tracking or third-party analytics on our surveys, and we do not add tracking scripts of our own to survey pages. On Formbricks we do not enable the platform's optional spam-protection feature, which would load Google reCAPTCHA. Cookies can be viewed, blocked or deleted through your browser settings. Blocking the cookies above may prevent a survey from working. Purpose of the processing of personal data The purpose of the collection, processing and use of the personal data mentioned above is: Conduct surveys, including the evaluation and reporting of the answers provided through the survey forms Produce the reports, deliverables, publications, strategies and roadmaps of EGI Foundation and of the projects it takes part in, using aggregated and anonymised results Contact you about your response, where you have given us your contact details for that purpose Establish that the results are sound, by identifying duplicate, automated or out-of-scope submissions and understanding which groups are represented in the responses Monitor and maintain the stability, performance and security of the survey platforms We do not use survey responses to build a profile of you, to make automated decisions about you, or to target advertising. Your responses are not sold. Legal basis The legal basis for processing personal data is: Legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party, Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest is in gathering and analysing the views of our community so that we can plan, evaluate and improve EGI Foundation's services, activities and strategy, and in keeping the survey platforms available, secure and free from automated and fraudulent submissions. You may object to this processing at any time using the contact details in the Data Protection Officer section. Compliance with a legal obligation, Art. 6 (1) (c) GDPR , for example the obligation to record personal data breaches and, where the conditions are met, to notify the supervisory authority and affected individuals, and the obligation to respond to your requests under Chapter III of the GDPR. Where a survey asks a question falling within Article 9 GDPR, the basis for that question is your separate explicit consent under Art. 9 (2) (a) GDPR, asked for at the question itself. Where a survey asks you to opt in to a further use, such as being contacted for a follow-up interview, the basis for that use is your consent under Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR, which you can withdraw at any time under Art. 7 (3) GDPR. Data processors and third parties to whom personal data is disclosed Personal data will not be used beyond the original purpose of their acquisition. Where a third party has to be involved in order to deliver the survey, that party acts as our processor on our documented instructions, under a contract meeting the requirements of Art. 28 GDPR, and only for the purposes set out in this policy. The data you provide will not be used for marketing and will not be sold. For the purpose given in this privacy policy, personal data may be passed to the following third parties. Within the European Union (EU) / European Economic Area (EEA) Formbricks GmbH (Kuhnkestr. 6, 24118 Kiel, Germany) for surveys using Formbricks, as data processor under a Data Processing Agreement incorporating the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses. Formbricks Cloud is hosted in Germany. Its sub-processors for this service are Amazon Web Services (Germany, database and e-mail infrastructure), Sentry (Germany, error tracking) and PostHog EU (Germany, product analytics on platform usage). Cloudflare provides the content delivery and security network through which the platform is served, and processes connection data including your IP address in transit; it does not receive or store your answers. LimeSurvey GmbH (Papenreye 63, 22453 Hamburg, Germany) for surveys using LimeSurvey and hosted on survey.egi.eu , as resource provider and sub-contracted data processor. The service is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH in Germany. Google LLC for surveys using Google Forms and hosted on docs.google.com/forms or forms.gle (resource provider, sub-contracted data processor). Survey managers , that is, the EGI Foundation staff and named project partners responsible for the survey concerned. Each survey states who they are. The records of your use and technical log files produced by the Service components may be shared, via secured mechanisms, for security incident response purposes with other authorised participants in the academic and research distributed digital infrastructures authorised by EGI Foundation governance, only for the same purposes and only as far as necessary to provide the incident response capability where doing so is likely to assist in the investigation of suspected misuse of Infrastructure resources. Outside the EU / EEA Survey managers located outside the EU or the EEA, where a survey is run jointly with a partner based outside Europe. Each survey states who they are. Such transfers take place under the conditions set out in Chapter V of the GDPR, normally an adequacy decision or Standard Contractual Clauses. Connection routing. The content delivery network serving the Formbricks platform directs your browser to the nearest available location on its network, so if you respond from outside Europe the connection may be handled outside the EU or the EEA. Only connection data is processed there, only for the moment the connection lasts, and your answers are stored in Germany in every case. EGI Foundation is confirming with the platform provider the safeguards applying to this routing, and will update this policy with the outcome. Any transfer of personal data to a third country outside the EU or the EEA must meet the conditions contained in Chapter V of the GDPR and comply with the provisions of this privacy policy and any related policies adopted by the EGI Federation. Where we identify such a transfer, we satisfy ourselves that those conditions are met before it continues, and we record it here. A survey may contain links to external websites, for example to a document you are being asked about. Those websites are operated by others and are outside our control. This privacy policy does not apply to them, and their own privacy notices apply once you follow a link. A survey platform may display its provider's own imprint and privacy policy at the foot of the page. Those documents describe how the provider handles data as a company and do not replace this policy, which is the one that governs your response. Your rights You can exercise the following rights at any time by contacting our data protection officer using the contact details provided in the Data Protection Officer section: Information about your data stored with us and their processing Correction of incorrect personal data Deletion of your data stored by us Restriction of data processing, if we are not yet allowed to delete your data due to legal obligations Objection to the processing of your data by us Data portability Withdrawal of your consent, where the processing is based on it (Art. 7 (3) GDPR), free of charge and without affecting processing carried out beforehand To act on a request about a specific response, tell us which survey it was and roughly when you responded, and give us any identifier the survey collected. Where a survey collected no identifier from you, we may be unable to find your response, and we will explain what we can and cannot do. How to raise a privacy concern If you have a question or a concern about how your personal data is handled, or if you wish to exercise any of the rights listed above, please contact our Data Protection Officer at dpo@egi.eu , using the postal address in the Data Protection Officer section above. You do not have to use any particular form of words, and there is no charge for making a request. We will acknowledge your request and respond to it without undue delay, and in any event within one month of receiving it. Where a request is complex, or where we have received a number of requests from you, we may extend that period by up to two further months, and we will tell you within the first month if this is the case and explain why. If we are unable to act on your request, we will tell you why and inform you of your right to complain to a supervisory authority and to seek a judicial remedy. If you no longer wish to be invited to EGI surveys, tell us at dpo@egi.eu or use the unsubscribe link in the invitation. This does not affect responses you have already given. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can complain at any time to the supervisory data protection authority (DPA) responsible for you. The responsible DPA depends on your country and state of residence, of your workplace or of the presumed violation. A list of the supervisory authorities with addresses can be found at edpb.europa.eu . You can contact EGI Foundation's lead supervising authority using the contact details provided in the Jurisdiction and supervisory authority section. Complaining to a supervisory authority does not affect any other remedy available to you. Children EGI surveys are addressed to researchers, professionals and members of the research and computing community, and are not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 16. Should a survey be aimed at a younger audience, for example in an outreach or training context, it will say so and we will obtain the consent required by Article 8 GDPR before any personal data is collected. If you believe a child has provided us with personal data through one of our surveys, please contact the Data Protection Officer and we will delete it. Data retention and deletion Data retention and deletion periods can vary for different surveys and are usually indicated on the survey form. By default: Answers submitted via a survey form are deleted or anonymised within six months of submission. Records of site usage and technical log files produced by the service components are deleted or anonymised after, at most, 18 months , as documented in EGI-doc 2732: Policy on the Processing of Personal Data . Aggregated and anonymised results are kept indefinitely, because they no longer identify anyone. Published reports, figures and anonymised quotations remain available after the underlying responses have been deleted. Contact details given for follow-up , such as an e-mail address for an interview or to receive the results, are deleted once the follow-up is complete and in any event within the same six months. Partial responses , where you began a survey and did not submit it, are kept only for the life of the survey and are deleted when it closes. Where a survey needs a longer period, its own statement gives the period and the reason. Deletion on the platform is followed by deletion from the provider's backups: on Formbricks, within 90 days. Our processors act only on EGI Foundation's documented instructions. If an agreement with a processor ends, the personal data is returned to EGI Foundation or deleted, at EGI Foundation's instruction. Security We take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure data security and the protection against accidental or unlawful destruction, accidental loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or access. Access to survey responses is limited to the survey managers who need it for the survey concerned, through named accounts with multi-factor authentication. A comprehensive overview of the technical and organisational measures taken by EGI Foundation can be found at EGI Document 3737: EGI Foundation Technical and Organisational Measures (TOM) . The measures applied by our platform providers are published by them: Formbricks at formbricks.com/security , which is audited to SOC 2 Type II. Personal data breaches A personal data breach is a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. We have procedures in place to detect, report and investigate such breaches. Our processors are required under their Data Processing Agreements to assist EGI Foundation in meeting its obligations under Articles 33 and 34 GDPR. Anyone can report a suspected breach or a security weakness affecting an EGI survey to the EGI Computer Security Incident Response Team (EGI CSIRT) at abuse@egi.eu , or to the Data Protection Officer at dpo@egi.eu . Reports made in good faith are welcome, and we will not pursue anyone who reports a weakness responsibly. Where a breach is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, EGI Foundation notifies the Dutch Data Protection Authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it. Where a breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we inform you without undue delay. All breaches are recorded in an internal register in accordance with Article 33 (5) GDPR, whether or not they are notifiable. Changes to this privacy notice We may update this privacy policy from time to time, for example if we change survey platform or if a platform configuration changes. Any change is published at this address and the version and date are revised. The policy that applies to your response is the one in force when you submitted it. Version 12 , 1 September 2026: EUSurvey removed, as it will no longer be accessible. Formbricks added as an alternative survey tool alongside LimeSurvey. Sections added covering how data is collected, anonymous and identified surveys, cookies, third-party websites, personal data breaches and children. Retention detail expanded. Code of Conduct reference corrected to REFEDS. Version 11 and earlier: available on request from dpo@egi.eu . Related policies EGI Foundation is conforming to REFEDS Code of Conduct and your personal data will be processed in accordance with the REFEDS Code of Conduct for Service Providers and the EGI-doc-2732-v3: Policy on the Processing of Personal Data . If we are unable to act on your request, we will tell you why and inform you of your right to complain to a supervisory authority and to seek a judicial remedy. If you no longer wish to be invited to EGI surveys, tell us at dpo@egi.eu or use the unsubscribe link in the invitation. This does not affect responses you have already given. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can complain at any time to the supervisory data protection authority (DPA) responsible for you. The responsible DPA depends on your country and state of residence, of your workplace or of the presumed violation. A list of the supervisory authorities with addresses can be found at edpb.europa.eu . You can contact EGI Foundation's lead supervising authority using the contact details provided in the Jurisdiction and supervisory authority section. Complaining to a supervisory authority does not affect any other remedy available to you. Children EGI surveys are addressed to researchers, professionals and members of the research and computing community, and are not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 16. Should a survey be aimed at a younger audience, for example in an outreach or training context, it will say so and we will obtain the consent required by Article 8 GDPR before any personal data is collected. If you believe a child has provided us with personal data through one of our surveys, please contact the Data Protection Officer and we will delete it. Data retention and deletion Data retention and deletion periods can vary for different surveys and are usually indicated on the survey form. By default: Answers submitted via a survey form are deleted or anonymised within six months of submission. Records of site usage and technical log files produced by the service components are deleted or anonymised after, at most, 18 months , as documented in EGI-doc 2732: Policy on the Processing of Personal Data . Aggregated and anonymised results are kept indefinitely, because they no longer identify anyone. Published reports, figures and anonymised quotations remain available after the underlying responses have been deleted. Contact details given for follow-up , such as an e-mail address for an interview or to receive the results, are deleted once the follow-up is complete and in any event within the same six months. Partial responses , where you began a survey and did not submit it, are kept only for the life of the survey and are deleted when it closes. Where a survey needs a longer period, its own statement gives the period and the reason. Deletion on the platform is followed by deletion from the provider's backups: on Formbricks, within 90 days. Our processors act only on EGI Foundation's documented instructions. If an agreement with a processor ends, the personal data is returned to EGI Foundation or deleted, at EGI Foundation's instruction. Security We take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure data security and the protection against accidental or unlawful destruction, accidental loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or access. Access to survey responses is limited to the survey managers who need it for the survey concerned, through named accounts with multi-factor authentication. A comprehensive overview of the technical and organisational measures taken by EGI Foundation can be found at EGI Document 3737: EGI Foundation Technical and Organisational Measures (TOM) . The measures applied by our platform providers are published by them: Formbricks at formbricks.com/security , which is audited to SOC 2 Type II. Personal data breaches A personal data breach is a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. We have procedures in place to detect, report and investigate such breaches. Our processors are required under their Data Processing Agreements to assist EGI Foundation in meeting its obligations under Articles 33 and 34 GDPR. Anyone can report a suspected breach or a security weakness affecting an EGI survey to the EGI Computer Security Incident Response Team (EGI CSIRT) at abuse@egi.eu , or to the Data Protection Officer at dpo@egi.eu . Reports made in good faith are welcome, and we will not pursue anyone who reports a weakness responsibly. Where a breach is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, EGI Foundation notifies the Dutch Data Protection Authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it. Where a breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we inform you without undue delay. children.main_text: Service Contracts EOSC EU Node (Procurement) EOSC EU Node (Procurement) The EOSC procurement builds and deploys a robust infrastructure, the EOSC EU Node, providing access to a diverse portfolio of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data and professional-quality interoperable services across various domains, including data handling, computing, processing, analysis, and storage. The procurement is structured into three areas, referred to as Lots. EGI strongly contributes to Lots 1 and 3. Development and Operation of the EOSC EU Node Leveraging its vast experience in federated services, EGI plays a crucial role in the design, architecture, delivery, and operation of the EOSC EU Node’s core services: Core Service Delivery : EGI contributes a substantial portion (nearly half) of the core services, forming the backbone of the EOSC EU Node. Key Components Integration : EGI’s contributions extend to critical components of the Authentication and Authorisation Infrastructure (AAI) and deliver one of the six integrated application services within the Node. Service Management System : EGI meticulously verifies and validates all components of the EOSC EU Node against industry standards and EOSC platform specifications. This ensures smooth integration and acceptance before deployment. Security Coordination : EGI spearheads security coordination for the EOSC EU Node. This includes crafting a comprehensive security plan and establishing robust procedures for handling potential security incidents. Contribution to Exchange Application Services : EGI provides Jupyter notebooks to facilitate interactive computing, enhancing researchers’ ability to analyse data and develop models within the EOSC ecosystem. Understanding the Needs of Research Communities – EGI’s extensive experience serving both individual scientists and large research communities is invaluable for the EOSC EU Node. EOSC EU Node (Website) EGI for EOSC LOT 1 Managed services for the development, integration, deployment and operations of the federated EOSC core platform EGI Foundation, together with partners GRNET and GWDG, is a participant in the ‘Open Science Agora Consortium,’ working alongside the lead partner Athena Research Centre, and joined by OpenAIRE AMKE, Netcompany-Intrasoft and GÉANT. EGI’s responsibilities will include the provision of: Monitoring and accounting frameworks, application workflow management, the helpdesk and the configuration management system IT services management framework and the onboarding of services Software verification and testing Single-Sign-On (SSO) Security coordination, including coordination of the risk management process for data protection EGI also contributes to communications, community outreach, and training activities to ensure strong user engagement Finally, EGI manages its subcontractors, GRNET and GWDG. GRNET’s responsibilities include PID management, SSO, monitoring, accounting for services, messaging, configuration management system, and verification and testing. GWDG will take the lead in PID management Funding + € 15.188.248 Start Date + 01 February 2024 End Date + 01 February 2027 LOT 3 Exchange application services Lot 3 procures file synchronisation and sharing service, interactive notebook service, and large file transfer service for the ‘EOSC Exchange’. In Lot 3, EGI and CESNET are members of a consortium led by EGI’s partner PSNC and participated by ownCloud, Safespring and NORDUnet. EGI Foundation’s support includes: the provisioning of Jupyter Notebooks (together with CESNET), and the overall service management coordination and integration with the services in other Lots Funding + € 6.000.000 Start Date + 01 February 2024 End Date + 01 February 2027 Related Projects EOSC Beyond EOSC Beyond: Advancing innovation and collaboration for research EOSC Data Commons EOSC Data Commons: Building a Collaborative Future for Research Data

children.main_text: Service Cloud Compute Run virtual machines on demand with complete control over computing resources Cloud Compute gives you the ability to deploy and scale virtual machines on-demand. It offers guaranteed computational resources in a secure and isolated environment with standard API access, without the overhead of managing physical servers. Get started Contact us Features Solutions Success Stories Providers Documentation Get started Overview Cloud Compute With Cloud Compute, you can deploy and scale virtual machines on demand. This means you’ll have guaranteed computational resources at your fingertips in a secure and isolated environment. Plus, with open API access, you can enjoy all the benefits of virtualisation without the overhead of managing physical servers. Main features Here are a few ways you can use Cloud Compute to enhance your workflow: Execute compute- and data-intensive workloads (both batch and interactive) with ease Host long-running services like web servers, databases, or application servers Create disposable testing and development environments on virtual machines and scale your infrastructure as necessary Select virtual machine configurations (CPU, memory, disk) to suit your needs Manage your Cloud Compute resources in a flexible way with integrated monitoring and accounting capabilities With EGI Cloud Compute, you can easily select pre-configured virtual appliances from our extensive catalogue, which is replicated across all EGI cloud providers. This means you can access a wide variety of computing resources without having to worry about maintenance, upgrades, or hardware failures. You can also scale up or down your computing resources based on your research needs, without disrupting your workflow. Riding the waves of success: How OBSEA leveraged EGI Cloud Compute OBSEA is a cutting-edge underwater observatory that revolutionises the exploration and comprehension of seas and oceans. As oceans are intricate and dynamic systems, a thorough understanding of their complexities is essential. OBSEA’s innovative approach involves gathering a high-resolution, multidisciplinary, long-time series collection of environmental variables that sheds light on the complexity of these vast bodies of water. The EGI Cloud Compute service plays a crucial role in ensuring scientific excellence by providing the necessary infrastructure to deploy data acquisition and data visualisation services. Consequently, the combination of OBSEA and EGI Cloud Compute service represents a significant advancement in oceanic research, providing invaluable insights into the mysteries of the world’s oceans. Read more Get started Trial access Try the service, prototype and validate applications and services. The EGI grant includes up to 4 vCPU cores, 8GB of RAM and 100GB of block storage. Custom access Long-term access, service level guarantees, dedicated support. Consultancy & Support Are you wondering if this service can help solving your challenges? Are you a user and seek support?
